notes: A practice hub with a course attached, and the hub is why this needs writing down. All 25 spawns are one point at [0 0 14416] in a room whose floor is 64x64x128 teleport pads, one per lettered sub-stage (stage1a..stage5k, 182 destinations) -- so a player can pad straight to any section. That is the map's own design and every server that has run it has zoned it the same way: the start line is the hub room, the finish is the finish. The finish itself is chained: five `*_stop` pads teleport to `end_stop`, which sits inside the one trigger aimed at the destination `end`, which throws you out of the course. Timing hub-to-end is therefore honest about the route and cannot be honest about a player who pads past half of it; a records server that cares should zone the sections as tracks instead.

conditional_teleports.note: the map's anti-standing trap: a trigger_multiple on each block sets the player's name to the one this filter passes after a delay and resets it after another, so the teleport only fires on a player who stood on a block too long. This game does not run the map's outputs, so imported unconditionally it fired on every landing. Dropped; standing still is allowed here and costs the player time instead

zones.note: the hub room, around the single point all 25 info_player_* entities share
the one trigger aimed at the `end` destination. `end_stop` -- where the five stage-stop pads land -- is a point inside this same volume, so both routes to the finish cross it
